title: Tata Sons Bets on AI and Semiconductors as FY26 Profit Surges 22%
excerpt: The conglomerate's annual report outlines a long-term strategy centered on chip manufacturing, artificial intelligence, aviation, and advanced manufacturing as standalone profit rises to ₹31,961 crore.
body:
• Tata Sons' standalone net profit rose 21.8% to ₹31,961 crore in FY26, with revenue growing 9.1% to ₹42,367 crore.
  • The broader Tata Group's consolidated profit surged 51.9% to ₹1,70,525 crore on revenue of ₹16.24 lakh crore.
  • Tata Electronics is building India's first high-volume semiconductor fab in Gujarat and has packaged the country's first indigenous microprocessor.
  • Chairman N. Chandrasekaran frames AI, semiconductors, aviation, and defense as the building blocks of "the India of 2047."

Tata Sons has laid out a sweeping roadmap centered on artificial intelligence, semiconductor manufacturing, aviation, and advanced manufacturing, according to its FY26 Annual Report. The holding company of the $185 billion Tata Group reported standalone net profit of ₹31,961 crore, up 21.8% year-on-year, on revenue of ₹42,367 crore.

At the group level, the numbers were more striking. Consolidated profit after tax surged 51.9% to ₹1,70,525 crore, while revenue rose 7.8% to ₹16,24,030 crore — 2.1 times and 5.4 times their FY20 levels, respectively. The board has recommended a final dividend of ₹1,10,717 per share, subject to shareholder approval.

The Semiconductor Play

The annual report's most significant disclosures center on Tata Electronics, which is constructing India's first high-volume semiconductor fabrication facility in Dholera, Gujarat. The company has already packaged India's first indigenous microprocessor and is developing advanced packaging capabilities, indigenous semiconductor materials, and working with cutting-edge lithography tools.

"The next industrial revolution is being designed and built right now, and its building blocks are silicon, connectivity, energy and security."

— N. Chandrasekaran, Chairman, Tata Sons

In four years, Tata Electronics has become the fourth-largest Tata Group company by revenue at ₹1,31,082 crore, with a workforce of 86,466 — nearly two-thirds of whom are women. The company manufactured 12% of the total volume of phones made by the global leader in 2025, and operating profits have already reached breakeven.

Chandrasekaran described semiconductors as "the new steel," arguing that no nation can afford to depend on others for what he called the most fundamental input of the modern economy.

AI Across the Group

The report frames the global AI investment cycle as a defining feature of 2026. Tata Consultancy Services, the group's IT flagship, has reached annualized AI revenue of $2.6 billion as of Q1 FY27 and announced the 1 GW HyperVault AI data center platform alongside partnerships with OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, and Anthropic. TCS's operating margin of 25.0% remains 404 basis points above the next best in the industry.

Chandrasekaran pushed back against perceptions that AI threatens the IT services industry. "India's technology industry built its global position by doing something many thought it couldn't: taking powerful new technologies and making them work, reliably and accountably, inside the world's most demanding institutions," he wrote. TCS plans to have as many AI agents as human employees within three years.

Aviation and Defense Milestones

Aviation remains a major strategic pillar. Air India, Tata Electronics, and Tata Digital continued to post losses during FY26, reflecting what the company called the high capital requirements and long gestation periods of these ventures. But Tata Advanced Systems delivered milestones: the "Made in India" C295 transport aircraft completed its maiden flight, and the company inaugurated India's first private-sector helicopter final assembly line for the Airbus H125, as well as its first overseas defense manufacturing facility in Morocco.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian professionals in the technology sector, the Tata Group's bets signal expanding career opportunities. TCS's aggressive AI hiring and Tata Electronics' fab project could create thousands of skilled positions, potentially drawing diaspora talent back to India. The group's combined market capitalization of $277 billion across 26 listed companies also makes it a significant component of India-focused investment portfolios.

Looking Ahead

The annual report signals that Tata Sons intends to continue deploying capital into emerging areas despite near-term losses. Chandrasekaran framed the investments as generational, pointing to the Tata Group's history of building institutions that took decades to prove themselves. "In 2047, the centennial of Indian independence, a young Indian will board an Air India plane, built with Indian components, chips fabricated on Indian soil, protected by defence systems built in India," he wrote.
